intro: API-OMNI-BRAIN is a local application: a daemon on 127.0.0.1:8799 plus a web interface that opens in its own window. It manages your free-tier API keys on your machine, probes models, ranks them and routes requests through a local OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible proxy. No key is shipped with the app; a key leaves your machine only toward the provider it belongs to.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: The first screen: counts of keys and catalogued models, per-application and per-provider usage of the last 24 hours, the status of the internal 'organs' (scanner, probes, router, ...), the best model per class and models that are currently resting after errors. The header shows the run state and has two buttons: scan now, and the emergency stop.
steps: Read the key and model counts and their status
See which applications and providers used the proxy in the last 24 hours
Look at the organ list to see when each part last ran
Use 'Scan and probe now' to start a scan, or 'All off' to stop routing

Show usage per application and provider over 24 hours
Show which models are resting and why
Start a scan on demand and switch everything off with one click
cannot: It does not start or stop the operating-system service (use systemctl --user)
It does not add, remove or test keys here (that is the Keys & Providers tab)

sections.title: Radar
sections.summary: Aggregates ~110 news feeds and 10 Hacker News searches every 2 hours, indexes ~2600 free-API entries with full-text search, re-checks models twice weekly, and matches use cases. Quarantined files are scanned, overwritten with zeros, and deleted with a popup; there is no release button.

Search the free-API index with full-text search

global_cannot: It is not an antivirus: the scanner uses signatures and heuristics; 'nothing found' is not 'proven harmless'.
It does not create accounts, buy anything, handle payments, trade, or move money.
It never writes into other programs' configuration itself (an agent changes its own configuration, only after you asked it to and approved it here).
It does not bypass rate limits, quotas, terms of service, CAPTCHAs, or paywalls.
It does not farm or share keys.
It does not crawl behind logins.
It cannot make a free API reliable: free tiers change, vanish, throttle; rankings are measurements of today.
It does not guarantee privacy at the provider: your prompts go to the provider you route to; their policies apply.
Search is only as good as the index; the judge model is coarse; the vision judge used for UI scoring is noisy (+-0.5 on a 10 scale).
Not tested on other distributions or Python versions than the listed ones (Linux x86_64 glibc >= 2.38, Python 3.12).
responsibility: You are responsible for obtaining and using API keys in accordance with each provider's terms of service. Your prompts are sent to the providers you route to; their privacy policies apply. Free tiers may change or vanish without notice; the app's rankings reflect measurements at the time of the scan. The app has only been tested on Linux x86_64 with glibc >= 2.38 and Python 3.12; other environments are unsupported.
